news.headline: uniQure Announces Submission of BLA for AMT-130, Gene Therapy Delivered via ClearPoint's Navigation Platform
news.summary: ClearPoint Neuro partner uniQure submitted a Biologics License Application to the FDA (plus a UK MAA) seeking accelerated approval of ifezuntirgene inilparvovec (AMT-130) for Huntington's disease, based on 3-year Phase I/II data; the therapy is surgically delivered using ClearPoint's Neuro Navigation System and SmartFlow MRI-safe cannula. A priority-review acceptance decision could follow within roughly eight months, and the filing is viewed as validating ClearPoint's CNS delivery platform ahead of what could be its first partner product approval.

news.headline: ClearPoint Neuro Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results, Cuts Full-Year Revenue Guidance
news.summary: Q2 2026 revenue was $10.9 million (+18% YoY), about $1.8 million below Street consensus, with net loss widening to $11.3 million ($0.38/share) as operating expenses rose 51% on IRRAS integration costs; cash fell to $29.4 million from $45.9 million at year-end 2025. Management cut FY2026 revenue guidance to $48-52 million (from $52-56 million) as it reprioritizes spending toward clinical case support, the new ClearPoint Advanced Laboratories (CAL) preclinical facility (where it signed its first GLP statement of work), and focused ultrasound/robotics/software development; shares fell roughly 15% after hours and several analysts cut price targets over the following days.

news.headline: ClearPoint Neuro Outlines Long-Term $500 Million Revenue Target and Five-Pillar Growth Strategy
news.summary: Alongside Q2 results, ClearPoint presented a long-term ambition to reach $500 million in annual revenue via a five-pillar strategy centered on cell and gene therapy delivery to the brain, citing 175+ active global centers, 60+ active biopharma partners across 15+ indications, and 10+ partner programs now under FDA expedited review. Management said it expects roughly 10 partner clinical trial data readouts over the next 18 months and that additional partner therapies could reach commercial approval as early as 2027.

news.headline: ClearPoint Neuro Congratulates Partner Aspen Neuroscience on FDA RMAT Designation for Sasineprocel
news.summary: The FDA granted Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy (RMAT) designation to Aspen Neuroscience's sasineprocel (ANPD001), an autologous dopaminergic cell therapy for Parkinson's disease delivered via the ClearPoint Navigation System in the ASPIRO trial, giving the program a faster regulatory pathway including potential accelerated approval.

news.headline: EpilepsyGTx Partners with ClearPoint Neuro for Targeted Delivery of Lead Gene Therapy in Epilepsy
news.summary: EpilepsyGTx selected ClearPoint's SmartFlow Cannula and Neuro Navigation System to deliver its gene therapy candidate EPY201 in an upcoming first-in-human Phase 1/2a trial for drug-resistant focal refractory epilepsy, adding another CNS gene-therapy partner to ClearPoint's biopharma ecosystem.

news.headline: ClearPoint Neuro Schedules Second Quarter 2026 Results for August 3, 2026
news.summary: ClearPoint Neuro confirmed it would report Q2 2026 financial results after market close on August 3, 2026, with a same-day conference call for investors and analysts, setting up the guidance-cut print that followed two weeks later.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings report
catalysts.detail: ClearPoint Neuro has not yet announced its Q3 2026 report date; based on prior-year timing (Q3 2025 results were released November 6, 2025), a similar November 2026 date is likely.

catalysts.label: FDA acceptance decision on uniQure's AMT-130 BLA
catalysts.detail: Following uniQure's September 2, 2026 BLA submission for AMT-130 (delivered via ClearPoint's platform), an FDA filing-acceptance decision and, if granted priority review, a target action date roughly eight months out would be a major validation event for ClearPoint's CNS delivery technology.

catalysts.label: Wave of partner clinical trial data readouts
catalysts.detail: Management said on the Q2 2026 call it expects roughly 10 partner clinical trial data readouts and 10-15 trials using ClearPoint technology enrolling patients over the next 18 months, arriving on an almost-monthly cadence.

catalysts.label: Potential partner BLA submissions / commercial approvals
catalysts.detail: Company cited positive FDA feedback to multiple biopharma partners on potential BLA submissions and said additional cell and gene therapies co-labeled with ClearPoint technology could reach commercial approval as early as 2027.

catalysts.label: First GLP statement of work at CAL preclinical facility completes
catalysts.detail: ClearPoint's newly acquired 30,000-sq-ft ClearPoint Advanced Laboratories (CAL) site in Torrey Pines signed its first Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) statement of work for an IND-enabling study, expected to complete in the first half of 2027 with more meaningful revenue contribution by late Q2 2027.

catalysts.label: Harmony 1.0 software and robotic platform launch
catalysts.detail: Product roadmap calls for Harmony 1.0 software with sub-nuclei segmentation in 2027, following 2026 navigation software/iCT upgrades, with a fuller robotic system (DBS/BCI area-of-activation modeling) targeted for 2028 and beyond.

pulse: ClearPoint Neuro's Q2 2026 print (August 3) was a clear miss and the FY2026 revenue guide was cut to $48-52M from $52-56M as the company shifts spending toward clinical support capacity, its new CAL preclinical facility, and R&D on focused ultrasound, robotics and software rather than pure sales expansion; shares dropped roughly 15% and analysts trimmed price targets, with cash down to $29.4M. Even so, the underlying biologics/CNS-delivery franchise kept adding validation: Aspen Neuroscience's RMAT designation, a new EpilepsyGTx gene-therapy delivery deal, and, most notably, partner uniQure's September 2 BLA submission for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease - a therapy delivered entirely through ClearPoint's Navigation System and SmartFlow Cannula. Management's long-range $500M revenue ambition rests on 60+ active biopharma partners and an expected wave of roughly 10 partner clinical data readouts over the next 18 months, so near-term execution and cash burn remain the key overhangs while the multi-year bet on becoming the default CNS delivery platform for cell/gene therapy partners looks intact and arguably strengthened by regulatory progress across multiple partner programs.
